- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) but underperform in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3), especially after recent spikes.
- Overshoots occur after strong upward sentiment or consecutive high prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in such cases.
- When sentiment turns negative or shows early signs of decline (e.g., 0.33 or below), model should adjust downward with a lag of 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast days (e.g., day 1–3 of 30d forecast) when sentiment is weak or mixed — use 2-day smoothing or lower volatility assumption.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.33 or below), reduce forecast by 5–10% across all days to avoid “overcorrection” bias.
